pr.title: Allow `inline(always)` with a target feature behind a unstable feature `target_feature_inline_always`.
pr.description:
Rather than adding the inline always attribute to the function definition, we add it to the callsite. We can then check that the target features match and that the call would be safe to inline. If the function isn't inlined due to a mismatch, we emit a warning informing the user that the function can't be inlined due to the target feature mismatch.

See tracking issue rust-lang/rust#145574
pr.author: JamieCunliffe

analysis.summary: The PR adds the `target_feature_inline_always` feature and a MIR lint pass, `CheckInlineAlwaysTargetFeature`, so `#[inline(always)]` may be used with `#[target_feature]` only when the caller has an effective target-feature set that makes the call safe to inline. Instead of unconditionally placing the alwaysinline attribute on the callee definition, codegen now places the inline attribute at the callsite when target features match; otherwise it omits the attribute and the MIR lint warns that the function will not be inlined.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `check_result` in `compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/codegen_attrs.rs` rejected the combination with `tcx.dcx().span_err(span, "cannot use `#[inline(always)]` with `#[target_feature]`")`, and `llfn_attrs_from_instance` in `compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/attributes.rs` computed the inline rule and unconditionally added it to the function definition with `to_add.extend(inline_attr(cx, inline));`. The feature description says: "Rather than adding the inline always attribute to the function definition, we add it to the callsite."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation is to treat removal of the hard error as the whole change: allow `#[inline(always)]` plus `#[target_feature]` while still emitting the alwaysinline attribute on the callee definition without checking the caller's effective target features. The PR's own rationale warns that "`#[inline(always)]` will always inline regardless of matching target features, which can result in errors from LLVM." The corrected transformation checks every direct call/tail-call, applies the inline attribute at the callsite only when `is_target_feature_call_safe` succeeds, and otherwise omits it and emits `INLINE_ALWAYS_MISMATCHING_TARGET_FEATURES`. A second incorrect variant is to omit the attribute silently after a mismatch; the PR instead requires the warning because "If the function isn't inlined due to a mismatch, we emit a warning informing the user that the function can't be inlined due to the target feature mismatch."
analysis.inputDomain: Rust function bodies containing MIR `Call` or `TailCall` terminators whose callee type is a statically known `ty::FnDef`, where the callee has codegen attributes with `inline == InlineAttr::Always` and non-empty `target_features`. The caller's effective features are its explicit `#[target_feature]` entries plus `tcx.sess.target_features` entries treated as `TargetFeatureKind::Implied`. Definitions without codegen attrs and indirect calls are skipped. The regression tests exercise aarch64 target features (`neon`, `fp16`, `sve`, `rdm`, `fhm`).
analysis.trigger: A direct call or tail call from a caller whose effective target features do not include all target features required by an `#[inline(always)]` callee, while the unstable feature `target_feature_inline_always` is enabled.
preconditions: The crate enables `#![feature(target_feature_inline_always)]`; without it the old combination remains a feature-gate error: "cannot use `#[inline(always)]` with `#[target_feature]`".
The callee is a `FnDef`, has codegen attrs, is marked `InlineAttr::Always`, and has a non-empty target-feature list.
The call is represented in MIR as `TerminatorKind::Call` or `TerminatorKind::TailCall`.
The caller's effective feature set includes both its explicit target features and the target's session-level features, the latter marked as implied.
For codegen, the function has user-defined target features, so the inline attribute is deferred from the definition to the callsite.
pitfalls: Do not simply delete the old error and keep function-definition alwaysinline: unsound inlining into a caller lacking required features is the reason the attribute is moved to the callsite.
Feature gating must remain: the check now uses `!tcx.features().target_feature_inline_always()` and emits a feature error rather than silently permitting the combination.

The inline-attribute helper still must preserve the invariant quoted as "`optnone` requires `noinline`": `OptimizeAttr::DoNotOptimize` must map to `InlineAttr::Never`, and `requires_inline` must still produce a hint.
The caller's effective feature set must include session target features as implied features; otherwise features supplied by the compilation target can produce false mismatch warnings.
When constructing the diagnostic's `callee_only` list, implied callee features are filtered out; tests should ensure the note and suggestion remain meaningful when filtering changes the list.

The MIR lint and the LLVM callsite check invoke `is_target_feature_call_safe` at separate sites with differently ordered operand expressions (callee features then caller features in the lint; `fn_call_attrs` then `fn_defn_attrs` in codegen), so both the warning behavior and the actual callsite attribute need coverage.
Only statically known `FnDef` callees are checked; indirect calls cannot be diagnosed by this pass and must not be assumed safe merely because no warning appears.
analysis.testStrategy: Use UI tests on a target with a real feature set, as the patch does with `//@[aarch64] compile-flags: --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `//@[aarch64] needs-llvm-components: aarch64`, plus `//@ add-core-stubs`, `//@ build-pass`, and `--crate-type=lib` with `#![feature(no_core, target_feature_inline_always)]`. Construct paired callers that differ only in their `#[target_feature]` declaration: a caller without features calling an alwaysinline `neon,fp16` callee must emit `inline_always_mismatching_target_features`; a caller with only a subset such as `fp16,sve` must still warn about the remaining `rdm`; a caller with matching or target-implied features must not warn. Also add a feature-gate test without the feature attribute expecting E0658. For codegen behavior, verify the inline attribute is applied at the callsite only in the matching case, while the callee definition omits it when user target features are present. No compiler was built in preparing this knowledge, so these are test-design recommendations rather than executed results.
